variables.name: lastSuccessfulRefresh
variables.description: Epoch time of the last completely successful forced dashboard refresh; never advanced by cache access or partial success.

variables.name: refreshing
variables.description: Guards whole-dashboard refreshes while their independent operations settle.

variables.name: loadResource
variables.description: Loads exactly one resource via its verified service method. Each rejection is caught locally and resolves false so parallel sections continue. Angular promise callbacks keep state digest-safe.

variables.name: isBusy
variables.description: Includes independent retries as well as the full refresh, keeping the top-right action disabled during any request.

variables.name: loadDashboard
variables.description: Starts all three resources concurrently; their promises catch errors independently. Only a fully successful forced refresh advances the complete-refresh timestamp.

variables.name: initializeDashboard
variables.description: Loads through service caches on entry; no shell or duplicate network transport is created.

variables.name: metricValue
variables.description: Formats only valid reported counts. Unknown, pending, failed and omitted fields remain an em dash; real zero is preserved.

variables.name: metricHint
variables.description: Explains loading, failure, missing inventory fields and successful data provenance without implying live availability.

variables.name: inventoryEmpty
variables.description: Missing reported status counts are an empty inventory snapshot, not zero inventory.
variables.body:
const state = $ctrl.resources.inventory;
return !state.loading && !state.error && state.value !== null && ['available', 'pending', 'sold'].every(key => !Object.prototype.hasOwnProperty.call(state.value, key));

variables.name: worldSummary
variables.description: Editorial count sentence derived solely from successful country records.

variables.name: destinationLink
variables.description: Uses registered nested states verbatim. Until destination children exist, follows the same agreed URL fallback as the confirmed workspace shell.
variables.body:
const state = 'workspace.' + section;
return $ctrl.$state.get(state) ? {type: 'state', state: state, parameters: {}} : {type: 'url', path: '#!/app/' + section, evaluate: false};

description:
## PetWorld overview
Dashboard child `workspace.home` at `/app/home`, rendered in the confirmed workspace outlet; navigation, main landmark and shell remain parent-owned.

Uses verified `petData` and `countryData` app services by opaque ID, with no page-level HTTP. Inventory, available pets and countries load concurrently through independently caught Angular promises. Each resource has its own loading/error/empty/retry state; failed or pending metrics display an em dash, never a fabricated zero. Inventory counts are independent server reports, not list totals. Featured cards show at most three actual records explicitly marked available. Country and unique continent counts derive from the successful normalized country dataset.

Refresh bypasses service caches and is disabled while any page request runs. Initial loads may use service caches. A last successful full refresh timestamp is recorded only after all three forced requests succeed; partial failures do not advance it. Individual retries do not reset other sections.

Reuses app-owned pw-stat-card, pw-pet-card and pw-feedback. Built-in Grid tracks use responsive CSS custom-property values for exact 1/2/4 metrics, 1/3 pets and 1/2 editorial panels; Box/Grid metadata owns structure. Core Badge supplies decorative paw/globe icons; no images, invented store locations or adoption claims.

The parent is confirmed. Destination child files were not available at creation: content links select exact workspace.pets/workspace.countries states when registered, otherwise use the parent shell's agreed #!/app/pets and #!/app/countries paths. The reused pet card owns its workspace.pet-detail link contract; that child must be registered by the app. No duplicate navigation is created.
